title: Check if String Is Decomposable Into Value-Equal Substrings
statement:
Call a string **value-equal** when all of its characters are the same digit: `"777"` and `"22"` qualify, `"121"` does not.

You get a string `s` made of digits. Decide whether `s` can be cut, from left to right, into consecutive value-equal pieces so that **exactly one** piece has length 2 and every other piece has length 3. Return `true` if such a cut exists, and `false` otherwise.
constraints: s contains only the digits '0' to '9'
notes:
## Intuition

A piece holds a single digit, so no piece can cross a spot where the digit changes. Each maximal run of one digit must therefore be split on its own into pieces of 3 and 2. A run of length `L` needs no 2-piece when `L % 3 === 0`, exactly one when `L % 3 === 2`, and at least two when `L % 3 === 1` (for example `4 = 2 + 2`, and `1` cannot be split at all). Since only one 2-piece is allowed in total, the answer depends only on the run lengths. Trying every way to cut the string also works, but it is slower and harder to get right.

## Approach

1. Keep `start`, the index where the current run began, and `pairs`, the number of runs that need a 2-piece.
2. Move `i` forward; while `s[i]` matches `s[start]` the run keeps growing.
3. When the run ends (a new digit or the end of the string), compute `runLength = i - start`.
4. If `runLength % 3 === 1`, return `false` at once.
5. If `runLength % 3 === 2`, add one to `pairs`. Then start the next run at `i`.
6. At the end, return whether `pairs === 1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "000111000"` has three runs: `"000"`, `"111"` and `"000"`, each with `runLength = 3` and remainder 0. None returns early and none adds to `pairs`, so `pairs` ends at 0 and the answer is `false`: there is no room for the single required 2-piece.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n), one pass over the string.
- Space: O(1), only a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- Exactly one 2-piece is required: a string whose runs are all multiples of 3 returns `false`.
- A run of length 4 or 7 is not fine just because it is long; remainder 1 always forces two 2-pieces.
- Do not forget the last run: the loop runs to `i === s.length` so the final run is measured too.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `start` | index where the current run of equal digits began |
| `i` | scan position; the run ends when `s[i]` differs or `i` reaches the end |
| `runLength` | length of the run that just ended |
| `pairs` | how many runs needed a piece of length 2 |

narration.2: Count the runs that need a piece of length 2; exactly one is allowed.
narration.3: The first run starts at index 0.
narration.4: Scan one step past the end so the last run is measured too.
narration.5: Is s[i] still the same digit as the start of the current run?
narration.6: Yes: the run keeps growing, so move on.
narration.8: The run just ended; measure its length.
narration.9: A remainder of 1 would need at least two pieces of length 2.
narration.10: That breaks the rule, so no cut exists.
narration.12: A remainder of 2 needs exactly one piece of length 2.
narration.13: Record that this run used the 2-piece.
narration.15: The next run begins where this one stopped.
narration.17: Valid only if exactly one run needed the 2-piece.
